To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a wage-profit frontier exists if and only if there exists a characteristic function that can be expressed in a certain way, and (b) given certain weak conditions, reswitching is possible if and only if the characteristic function can be expressed in another way, and (c) if the characteristic function is expressible in either way, then the inequality mentioned above holds, and (d) the characteristic function can embody nontechnical relationships.

(i) the existence of a frontier implies the existence, in a technology, of functional relationships among technical parameters, (ii) these relationships can be expressed in the form of characteristic functions, (iii) the characteristic functions can be used to order the techniques in a technology, and (iv) the characteristic functions are not necessarily independent of the “exogenous” relationships that determine which techniques belong to the technology.

the wage-profit frontier implies a characteristic function, that the existence of the characteristic function implies the existence of a functional relation between the technical parameters, that the functional relation between technical parameters can be used to determine the order of techniques, and that the functional relation can embody nontechnical factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the implications of the existence of a technological frontier for the theory of the firm, and with the possibility of incorporating nontechnical considerations into the theory of the technological frontier.
the implications of the existence of a frontier for the structure of the production function, and with the implications of this structure for the theory of capital and income distribution.
the implications of the wage–profit frontier for the theory of production.

the existence of the frontier implies that the technology is characterized by functional relationships among the parameters, and these functions can be expressed in a variety of forms, depending on the particular characteristics of the technology.

the wage-profit frontier is a necessary condition for the existence of a technology, and that a technology is a necessary condition (but not a sufficient one) for the existence of reswitching of technique.
a wage-profit frontier is a necessary condition for the existence of a technology, and that the wage-profit frontier and the characteristic functions together are sufficient conditions.

the existence of an equilibrium relation between the profit and wage rates implies a set of functional relationships that determine the characteristics of the techniques that are to be considered in the analysis.
